speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In August 2022, I spoke about the need for us to prioritise the safety of every worker, as companies sought to clear the backlog of work caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In September 2023, I spoke about the importance of keeping workplaces safe beyond the heightened safety period.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My speech today will focus on an aspect of WSH that is often overlooked.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This aspect of WSH is not as acute as workplace injuries and fatalities but can become as debilitating as injuries and mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am referring to Occupational Diseases (ODs), a "silent terror" at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: ODs are health conditions caused by risk factors at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: ODs not only cause debilitating effects but can have lasting negative effects on a worker's earning ability, productivity and employability.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Some examples of ODs include noise-induced deafness due to exposure to excessive workplace noise and work-related musculoskeletal disorder due to physical factors, such as lifting heavy loads or working in awkward postures for extended periods of time.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: These two types of ODs made up more than 90% of our local OD cases reported in 2023 and the first half of 2024.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Often, the worker's condition and symptoms will only show at a later stage after prolonged exposure to workplace risks and some could be mistaken for the side effects of ageing.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, I wish to present some suggestions on how the Government and the industry can better prevent, detect and deal with OD cases at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: First, workplace health surveillance efforts should be expanded and more stringently enforced to ensure early detection and to tackle under-reporting of ODs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I earlier mentioned that Singapore was seeing a rising trend of OD cases.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: MOM has attributed the increase to the Enhanced Workplace Health Surveillance efforts, also known as the WHS+.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I believe that the increase in OD cases that we have seen is only the tip of the iceberg.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: WHS+ is currently focused on workers' exposure to excessive noise and chemical hazards.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Sectors surveyed are limited to those in industrial settings, such as in construction.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But we must not forget that workers in other workplace settings, such as food and beverage outlets that play persistent loud music, and call centres where the operators have to put on headsets throughout the day during work, may also be exposed to excessive noise, as experts have recently reported in a CNA article.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I therefore urge MOM to expand WHS+ to require more companies and industries to undergo surveillance for excessive noise.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Surveillance under WHS+ should also be expanded to cover other types of OD, beyond noise.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One example is what I have described earlier, work-related musculoskeletal disorder, the second-highest reported OD category in Singapore over the past three years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Work-related musculoskeletal disorder is not restricted to any sector but can affect workers across diverse work environments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Office workers may unknowingly suffer from this disorder due to poor posture and doing repetitive activities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In healthcare, workers are subject to heavy loads due to shifting and assisting patients, which can lead to back injuries.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Our taxi drivers and bus captains also tell me that they experience back pain from prolonged sitting.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Expanding the scope of surveillance to include other ODs would enable early detection and facilitate timely treatment of conditions before they worsen.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, the Workplace Safety and Health (Medical Examinations) Regulations specifies certain occupations in the First Schedule that are subject to periodic medical examinations due to the risks of ODs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In doing so, the Government can leverage the wide network of Healthier SG general practitioner (GP) clinics to ensure that our healthcare system would not be overloaded.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mandatory health screenings will also go a long way in tackling the issue of under-reporting of OD cases.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: According to global research on ODs, there are many reasons for under-reporting of OD.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For example, workers may not seek immediate medical attention from their workplace doctor because of a mild discomfort.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Workers may also turn to a GP for temporary symptom relief, not understanding that the root cause of their pain was due to work.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The potential hefty costs of having to see a specialist is another possible reason that could deter some from seeking treatment early.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should conduct local studies to examine the prevalence of under-reporting of ODs locally.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope that MOM will study and investigate all possible reasons for under-reporting of OD cases here in Singapore and take measures to plug the gap.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For example, the United Kingdom (UK) collects its WSH data from a wide variety of sources, including voluntary reporting of anonymised cases by specialist doctors and self-reported data through its labour force survey.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is in addition to data from its compulsory reporting regime.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We can learn from the UK and other countries how they collect and use additional data points to investigate the prevalence of OD.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope MOM will review how we in Singapore collect data on OD cases, with a view of reducing under-reporting.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Timely, relevant and accurate data is crucial to help us assess the extent of OD in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The use of technology can aid the early detection of OD risk factors at work and improve work processes to reduce workers’ exposure to OD risks.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This includes the use of automation to limit human exposure, as well as preventive surveillance of risk factors.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As the popular proverb goes, “prevention is better than cure.” We must start by trying to prevent ODs from occurring in the first instance.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Employers have an onus in preventing ODs, by providing workers with the appropriate equipment and a safe working environment.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is a widely accepted principle in many countries, such as the United States and the UK, where obligations are placed on employers to help workers deal with the inherent risks associated with the work that they perform.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Here, I would like to highlight the proactive efforts of KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) as an example of such preventive surveillance.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The hospital has identified work-related musculoskeletal disorders as an issue affecting its healthcare workers and took measures to address this using technology.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Thermal imaging has no known negative health side effects, but it adds also a layer of privacy as it does not allow for the identification of an individual.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This allows risk factors leading to the disorder to be detected without compromising privacy concerns.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Such projects and innovations can help to uplift the safety standards, but I acknowledge that not all companies have the same investment capabilities as KKH.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As such, I call on the Government to provide more funding support for more companies to innovate and adopt technological solutions to reduce workers’ exposure to OD risks.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is especially important for workers, who might not understand the impact that their jobs have on their health.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must educate our workers on the dangers of OD and place an emphasis on younger workers before prolonged exposure to OD risks causes irreparable damage to their health in the years ahead.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Therefore, it is timely to review and update these guidelines to ensure that they remain relevant and effective.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Singapore has numerous medical facilities and research institutes specialising in occupational health and disease.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This Centre would serve to galvanise all research on the various ODs, with a focus on our local context and, more importantly, consolidate resources for more effective public education on OD.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope the Government will also ramp up efforts to educate employers and workers on the long-term dangers of OD, and I invite employers to work with NTUC to identify and address OD risks at your specific workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I would therefore like to, once again, call on the Government to mandate the need for a WSH representative in all companies.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have been repeating this proposal for many years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Having a mandatory WSH representative in all companies will allow MOM to impose an audit requirement, where every company, no matter how big or small, would need to take time to take care, just to borrow the tagline of the WSH Council, to examine if the work that they do can subject their workers to the risk of OD.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must also tap on existing expertise to develop more targeted, industry-specific guidance to reduce OD across all industries.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the area of WSH, our emphasis has always been on safety, as any mishap there can be immediate and acute.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, ODs, if not dealt with, can have a long-lasting impact on workers’ productivity and health span.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Workplace safety and health; it is time we pay equal emphasis on health as we do in safety.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Labour Movement stands ready to partner with all our tripartite partners to tackle ODs for a healthier workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While he was speaking, some Members have reminded me they have been here for 11 hours and therefore, they asked if the Member can also advocate for shorter Parliamentary Sittings, so that we can reduce the risk of ODs for Members in Parliament!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On a more serious note, tackling ODs is crucial for achieving a healthier and more resilient workforce in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Every worker deserves a safe and healthy work environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I share the Member’s views that the latent nature of ODs is a major challenge in tackling them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This makes it a lot harder to pinpoint the source of ODs, such as noise-induced deafness or musculoskeletal disorder, which develop over time as workers move across different worksites or different employers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Employers may also attribute workers’ ODs to non-work-related sources, such as personal lifestyles or ageing, and this makes for a complex issue, which goes beyond the lack of awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I will touch on how we are addressing these challenges here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, we are strengthening our surveillance efforts to enable early detection and prevention of occupational diseases before they start to affect workers’ health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under the Enhanced Workplace Health Surveillance programme, companies with work processes that are noisy or involve toxic substances must monitor the noise or chemical levels of their workplace environments respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Such designated companies must also send their workers for statutory medical examinations to detect early signs of ODs, such as deterioration of hearing or elevated levels of heavy metals in the body.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If any worker is found to be exposed to excessive noise or chemicals, the company must implement risk control measures immediately to protect their workers’ health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Companies with excessively high exposure levels must also undergo third-party audits to ensure the effectiveness of their workplace health programmes and these audit reports would have to be submitted to MOM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The increased numbers are due to our enhanced surveillance rather than more reporting, but it also shows that it shows up in our numbers as we enhance our enforcement efforts or inspection efforts, and through reporting to the hospitals and polyclinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hence, we are more targeted, we are more focused and therefore, we hope to intervene a lot quicker in specific sectors that are causing ODs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As suggested by the Member, the Government is also supporting companies to apply appropriate technologies that can help monitor and reduce workers’ exposure to OD risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM publicises the use of such technology solutions on its website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The solutions include digital wearable devices, which can provide real-time monitoring of workers’ health, detect biomechanics and alert workers when they adopt unsafe postures or are exposed to body vibration transmitted from work tools for prolonged periods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Employers could then use the data collected by such digital wearable devices to pinpoint specific work activities and implement necessary interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Additionally, employers can use sound level meters to monitor the noise level real-time, so that they can implement measures to ensure that the noise levels do not exceed pre-set thresholds, thereby lowering the risk of hearing loss among workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM and the WSH Council have developed and published several industry guidelines, including guidelines on the diagnosis and management of ODs, guidelines on hearing conservation programme and guidelines on improving ergonomics in the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Companies may refer to the guidelines on workplace ergonomics to tackle work-related musculoskeletal disorders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also partnered the WSH Council to promote good workplace practices, such as installing noise barriers or insulation to reduce the noise emitted from machines, as well as switching to the use of safer chemicals for work processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Apart from educating employers in high-risk industries, we collaborated with the Ministry of Health (MOH) to raise awareness in the medical community to detect and report ODs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is very similar to what the Member shared earlier of what other countries, such as the UK, are doing, where we work with medical practitioners at hospitals and our polyclinics of the importance of reporting ODs to MOM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this is also circulated by joint circulars by both Ministries, MOM and MOH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this contributes towards MOM’s OD monitoring efforts and informs us on which OD we should target.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, taking in all the joint data from our polyclinics and hospitals enables us to do, watch trends, to look at sources and what kind of interventions might be needed and where the sources would be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Tripartite Committee on Workplace Health also recently established a sub-committee on occupational health comprising representatives from healthcare, Government, businesses and worker groups to improve the detection, prevention and management of ODs in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is not a task that we can achieve on our own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will require the combined efforts of corporate leadership, industry associations, the medical community, union leaders and workers – and all of us here in this room.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together, we can protect our workforce from the dangers of these “silent killers” and make our workplaces safer and healthier for all of us.
